stem: During a hospital fire response, staff move patients from the affected area through a protected horizontal exit into another protected portion of the same building on approximately the same level. What type of evacuation is this?
rationale: A horizontal exit provides a protected path from one building area to another on approximately the same level. Moving occupants across that protected separation is horizontal evacuation rather than vertical or external evacuation.
educational_objective: Identify horizontal evacuation through a protected horizontal exit during a health-care fire response.
source_organization: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) / U.S. Access Board
source_document_title: Life Safety Code Survey Guidance — Horizontal Exits; Guide to the ADA Accessibility Standards
source_version_date: CMS 2786T K0226 revision 2026-02-01; current Access Board guidance
source_locator: CMS K0226 Horizontal Exits; Access Board Chapter 4 — Horizontal Exits
source_claim_supported: Horizontal exits allow movement into another protected area on approximately the same level and support horizontal evacuation.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8/PDF p.12
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — emergency response and evacuation
correction_summary: Defined the movement using current CMS horizontal-exit survey guidance and the Access Board rather than an unsourced generic fire-safety label.
